account:
Today the only unusual matter I have learned of is a vague rumor about changes to the bridge or port. I have not seen evidence of such changes, and I do not know what they would be for. Our neighbour at the east-bank cottage mentioned hearing the rumor but said they had seen nothing unusual and gave no source. The secretary traced a named link to Townsfolk 03, who directed her to the innkeeper; the innkeeper denied proposing or announcing any change. I have asked the secretary to arrange a conversation with Townsfolk 03 tomorrow, without displacing my appointments, to hear their account directly.

The available practical reports suggest ordinary business rather than an established emergency. The neighbour reported quiet docks, Freight offering ferry rides and deliveries, and the baker preparing fresh bread for market with no special celebration planned. The secretary's written accounts record says the builder found the bridge passable with no confirmed defects and relayed Freight's report of undamaged roads and a trouble-free morning ferry crossing. Those are reports, not my own inspections. The builder has also been asking people about specific repair needs and offering written estimates before work. No definite repair need, claim, receipt, or approved spending has been established.

I attended tea at the neighbour's cottage and returned to the office, though later than my scheduled half-past-four appointment. The secretary filed the accounts record and clarified which cottage the tea appointment meant. She reported no additional correspondence or business and agreed to have the appointment book ready for my morning review. I came home for the scheduled seven-o'clock engagement and have waited until eight; nobody has appeared or spoken to me here. For now, I suspect the bridge-and-port talk may simply be an unsupported rumor, but its origin and purpose remain unknown. I have no grounds to conclude that anyone is organizing a hidden project or acting against the town.
